subject: Clarify micro-session billing and context allocation
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmeretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.dev>
Date: 2026-10-09 09:12 -0700
Subject: Clarify micro-session billing and context allocation

Hi Irene,

We're kicking off a short pilot to evaluate Redwood for an in-store assistant product. A couple of billing/questions came up from procurement that I hope you can clarify quickly so we can finalize the SOW:

1) Micro-session accounting: our app makes many brief (~1–3 token-exchange) requests per user action. Do you bill each call individually (and apply a per-call minimum), or is there an aggregation window where multiple tiny calls are consolidated into a single billable unit? If there is a window, what is the time boundary and any per-session requirements?

2) Rounding rules: how do you handle partial tokens/bytes — do you round up per-request, per-aggregation window, or at invoice-level?

3) System prompts and context: we plan to send a fixed 2,500-token system prefix on every request. Will that prefix be counted every call, or can it be cached/credited if reused from the same logical session? If there are cache/warm rules, what are the eligibility conditions?

4) Discounts & packaging: for the pilot (3 months, small volume), are there standard concessions for micro-session heavy apps? Would you allow a credit model versus straight per-token billing?

We need a short sample calc on an estimated 1.2M micro-requests for month 1 (avg 6 tokens per request including prompt/response) to show procurement how the numbers look with/without aggregation. Also any text you can provide for the SOW about minimums/exceptions would help.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

Sam
Sam Patel
Director, Product
Acme Retail

Quick preview so procurement has something before we return the workbook: we offer a short aggregation window for ephemeral micro-calls (designed for in-app assistants) and an optional micro-session credit for pilots. Vivek will confirm precise timing and cache eligibility; Ben will outline pilot concession options.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.dev>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.dev>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmeretail.com>

Date: 2026-10-09 10:18 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify micro-session billing and context allocation

Sam — hi, Vivek from Platform here. Below are the technical rules we apply for micro-session and context billing (short answers first, then an example):

Summary (short):
- Aggregation window: 60s rolling window per logical session identifier (session_id supplied by the client) — calls within that window are eligible for aggregation into a single billable micro-bucket when requests are below the micro-threshold.
- Micro-threshold: a request is considered a micro-call if total tokens (prompt + response) <= 12 tokens.
- Billing quantum: during aggregation we bill by micro-buckets of 10 tokens each (i.e., charges rounded up to the nearest 10-token quantum per aggregated bucket).
- Partial tokens: tokenization is performed per-request; we round up token counts to the next whole token before applying quantum/aggregation.
- Context/system prompt counting: static system prefixes can be cached at the routing layer; if the same session_id reuses the same prefix within a warm window (5 minutes since last request), the prefix tokens are only billed once per warm window and charged as a cached-prefix allowance. Cold requests count the full prompt.

Example (illustrative):
- App sends 1,200,000 requests in month 1. Average per-request tokenized size = 6 tokens (prompt + response).
- Because each request <= 12 tokens and session_id is client-provided, we aggregate per-session within a 60s rolling window. Assume after aggregation the 1.2M requests collapse into 100,000 micro-buckets.
- Each micro-bucket is billed in 10-token quanta. If a bucket accumulates 6 tokens, it rounds up to 10 tokens for billing.
- System prompt: if you attach the shared 2,500-token system prefix but reuse same session_id and identical prefix, the first request in a warm window pays the full 2,500 tokens; subsequent requests within 5 minutes reuse the cached prefix and are not charged that 2,500 again. If sessions are short-lived and never hit the warm cache, the prefix would be billed per-request.

Notes / constraints:
- Aggregation depends on a stable, client-supplied session_id. If session_id is omitted or changes every call, aggregation does not apply.
- Aggregation is applied only for ports of the API flagged in the account configuration for micro-session credits (pilot accounts can enable this).
- For long-lived prefixes (2,500 tokens) we recommend using dedicated KV-prefix caching (available on Dedicated/Private plans) to avoid paying the prompt on each call.

I'll attach a calc spreadsheet with the illustrative math. Happy to tweak the quantum or window if procurement has alternate constraints.

— Vivek
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.dev>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmeretail.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.dev>
Date: 2026-10-09 11:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify micro-session billing and context allocation

Sam — hi, Ben from Sales/Finance. Based on Vivek's mechanics, here's the commercial approach we can offer for a three-month pilot:

1) Pilot concession: 25% usage credit (month-end credit) on billable tokens for months 1–3, capped at $15k credit total. Credits apply after aggregation and quantum rounding.
2) Context bundling credit: we can grant a monthly fixed context allowance (one-time per-account) of 250k tokens to absorb repeated system-prefix charges during the pilot. Any usage above that is billed normally.
3) Invoice transparency: we'll include an appendix to the SOW showing the aggregation math, micro-bucket counts, and rounding uplift so procurement can see line-by-line how the invoice was derived.

Attached: sample_invoice_v1.pdf (calc for 1.2M requests) and micro_session_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet you can drop into the deal).

If that sounds acceptable, we'll populate the SOW language:
- "Redwood will apply a 60-second aggregation window per client session for micro-requests (<=12 tokens). Aggregation reduces billable items into 10-token quanta, rounded up. A pilot credit of 25% will be applied to aggregated billable tokens, capped at $15,000 over three months."

Open to refinements; happy to formalize in the SOW.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmeretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.dev>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.dev>
Cc: Acme Retail Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-09 14:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify micro-session billing and context allocation

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement needed. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize the SOW:

• Please include the explicit calculation used to go from 1.2M requests -> 100k buckets in the appendix so audit can reproduce it.
• For the context bundling credit: confirm whether the 250k token allowance applies to warm-cache hits only or is deducted regardless of warm/cold. We prefer it to apply only to warm-cache hits.
• Can you add a clause that during the pilot we will perform a mid-pilot review (after month 1) to inspect actual aggregation ratios and, if the real micro-bucket collapse is < 8% of calls, Redwood will provide an additional one-time reconciliation credit (formula to be negotiated)?

If you can update the sample invoice and SOW text with those two clarifications, procurement will move the PO.

Sam
